title: Work and my day
cando: say what you do, when you work, and what you do every day

about.text: This lesson is about work. You say your job and times. You say what you do every day.
goals: Say your job: I'm a teacher.
Say where you work: I work at a hospital.
Say your times: I start at eight.
Use in the morning, at night, on Monday.
Read work hours and opening times.

chapters.title: What do you do?
chapters.text:
This lesson is about your work.
First, two people meet. They are Lena and Samir.
Lena asks: What do you do?
Samir says: I'm a cleaner. I work at the hospital.
Then she asks: What time do you start?

chapters.title: I'm a cleaner
chapters.text:
Say a before your job. I'm a cleaner. Not: I'm cleaner.
Say at before a time. I start at eight.
In the morning. In the afternoon. In the evening.
But: at night. And days: on Monday, on Sunday.

chapters.title: Hours and days off
chapters.text:
Next, read a notice at a café.
It has work hours and days off.
It has opening times too.
Then write about your day and week.

chapters.title: A new person at work
chapters.text:
A new person comes to your work.
Say your job and your hours. Say your day off.
Then ask: And you?

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a short story. It is about work.
Read it once for the story. Then read it again.

warmup.prompt: When do you like to work?
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. Some people like the morning. Some people work at night.

conversation.title: What do you do?
conversation.setting: Lena and Samir live in the same street. They meet at the bus stop.
lines: Hello. I'm Samir. Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you too. What do you do?
I'm a cleaner. I work at the hospital.
I start at ten at night.
Yes. I finish at six in the morning. And you?
I'm a shop assistant. I work at Kwame's Shoes.
I start at nine in the morning.
No. Sunday is my day off.
Oh, here's your bus. Goodbye, Lena!

questions.why: Samir says: I start at ten at night.
Lena says: Sunday is my day off.

phrases.use: Saying your job. Say a before the job.

phrases.text: I start at ten at night.

phrases.use: Saying the day you do not work.

items.meaning: The work you do for money.
To do a job, for money.
items.example: I work at a big hotel.

items.meaning: A person who helps people learn.
Their job is to drive. They drive buses or taxis.
Their job is to clean. They clean offices or homes.
items.example: I'm a cleaner at the hospital.
I'm a student. I'm learning English.

items.meaning: They help people in a shop.
A clock shows it. Now it is eight.
The first part of the day. Before twelve.
items.example: I start at eight in the morning.

items.meaning: It is dark. Many people sleep.

sound.title: The -er in teacher
sound.explain: The end of teacher is short and quiet. Driver and cleaner end the same way. So do mother and father. Listen, then say each group.

sayIt.instructions: Say Samir's lines. Record yourself, then listen back. Is your voice clear?
lines: Hello. I'm Samir. Nice to meet you.
I'm a cleaner. I work at the hospital.
I start at ten at night.
Yes. I finish at six in the morning. And you?

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation.
examples: I start at ten at night.
I start at nine in the morning.
spot.question: Which small word comes before the job? Which word comes before a clock time? Which words come before morning, night and Sunday?
spot.answer: A comes before the job: I'm a cleaner. At comes before a clock time: at ten, at nine. Then: in the morning, at night, on Sunday.

rules.title: Jobs and times
rule: A job: I am a teacher. He is a driver.
A time: I start at eight. I finish at four.
in the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening
at night, on Monday, on Sunday
Ask: What do you do? What time do you start?
rules.mistake: Not: I am teacher. Say: I am a teacher. Not: in the night. Say: at night.

practice.why: Say a before a job: I'm a teacher.

practice.q: He's a ___ . He drives a bus.
practice.why: A driver drives a bus or a taxi.
At before a clock time: at eight.

practice.q: I finish at four ___ the afternoon.
A: What do you ___ ? B: I'm a cleaner.
practice.why: What do you do? asks about your job.

practice.q: A: What ___ do you start? B: At nine.
practice.why: What time asks about the clock.

practice.q: I ___ work at six in the evening. Then I go home.
My day ___ is Saturday. I don't work.
practice.why: A day off: a day with no work.

yourTurn.prompt: Say your job and your times. Write three or four short lines.
starters: I start at … . I finish at …
yourTurn.model: I am a shop assistant. I work at a shoe shop. I start at nine in the morning. I finish at five in the afternoon.

text.title: Hours and days off
text.body:
PRACTICE NOTICE: not a real café

GREEN LEAF CAFÉ
Hours and days off

Carlos: 7 to 3. Days off: Sunday, Monday
Priya: 3 to 11. Days off: Saturday, Sunday
Ill? Call Omar before 7 in the morning.

OPENING TIMES
Monday to Friday: 7 to 11
Saturday: 8 to 11
Sunday: closed

gist.a: work hours, days off and opening times
gist.why: It says: Hours and days off. Then: Opening times.

detail.q: What time does Carlos start work?
Carlos is ill. What does he do?
detail.why: Ill? Call Omar before 7 in the morning.

detail.q: Is the café open on Sunday?

items.example: I finish at four in the afternoon.

items.meaning: The end of the day, before night.
items.example: I'm at home in the evening.

items.meaning: From morning to night. A week has seven.

items.example: I work five days a week.

model.title: My day and my week
model.body:
I am a cleaner.
I work at a hospital.
I start at ten at night.
I finish at six in the morning.
I sleep in the afternoon.
I work five days a week.
My days off are Saturday and Sunday.

write.task: Write about your day and your week. It can be real or made up. Copy the model. Then change the words.
write.starter: I am a … . I work at …
checklist: I wrote a before my job: I am a …
I wrote at before the times: at eight.
I used in the morning, in the evening or at night.

card.title: A new person at work
card.situation: You work at a hotel. Tomasz is new at your work. You meet him at the start of the day.
card.goal: Tell Tomasz your job, your hours and your day off. Then ask: And you?

phrases: I start at seven in the morning.
I finish at three in the afternoon.
prepare.notes: Write your job, your start time, your finish time and your day off.

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, your teacher is new at your work. Say your job, your hours and your day off. Then ask: And you? Then change roles.
doIt.wehel: You are new at my work. Ask me: What do you do? What time do you start and finish? When is your day off? Then I ask you the same questions. Use very short, simple sentences.

model.title: A new person at work
lines: Hi. I'm Tomasz. I'm new here.
Hello, Tomasz. I'm Ana. Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you too. What do you do?
I'm a driver. I drive the hotel bus.
I start at seven in the morning.
My day off is Sunday. And you?
compare: Did you say your job with a: I'm a …?
Did you say when you start and finish, with at?
Did you say your day off?

canDo: I can say my job: I'm a cleaner.
I can say when I start and finish work.
I can say in the morning, at night and on Monday.
I can read work hours and opening times.
I can tell a new person at work my job and my day off.

reading.before: Look at the title and the first picture. What is the person's job? What time is it?
reading.talk: What do you do every day? What do you do on your day off? Write two or three sentences, or say them to Wehel.

quiz.q: I'm ___ driver. I drive a bus.
quiz.why: Say a before a job: I'm a driver.
At before a clock time: at nine.

quiz.q: A: What do you do? B: ___
quiz.why: What do you do? asks about your job.

quiz.q: Lena helps people in a shop. She is a shop ___ .
quiz.why: A shop assistant helps people in a shop.

quiz.q: After twelve, before the evening: the ___ .
The shoes are too ___ . Can I have a smaller size?
quiz.why: Too big, so you want a smaller size.
Say I am tired, not I have tired.

quiz.q: She says: Go right. You check: ___
quiz.why: Say the same word back, to check.

liveClass: Day 1: a jobs round. Each learner says: I'm a … . I work at … . Then practise the bus stop conversation in pairs, and change the jobs and the times.
Day 2: the real-life task. You are new at each learner's work. Each learner says their job, their hours and their day off, and asks: And you?
Day 3: talk about the book. Then each learner says one thing they do in the morning and one thing in the evening.
